description: A two-panel composite figure of mechanical-property data for Fe-Mn-Al-C (printed as FeeMneAleC) low-density steels; both panels are property curves, no micrographs. (a) plots "Charpy impact absorbed energy, J" (y-axis, 0-250 J, ticks every 50 J) against "Testing temperature, °C" (x-axis, -200 to 100 °C). Five numbered curves are drawn over four shaded reference bands labelled "Austenite stainless steel" (upper), "Dual phase steel", "Ferrite steel" and "Martensite steel" (lower right). Curves 1 and 2 (open squares) rise from roughly 60-70 J at about -190 °C to 150-170 J near -110 °C and approach 200 J near 0-20 °C; curve 3 (open diamonds) rises almost linearly from near 0 J to slightly above 200 J at 20 °C. Curves 4 (filled squares) and 5 (filled triangles) remain below about 50 J over the whole range and fall to near 0 J at room temperature. (b) plots "Impact toughness, J/cm2" (y-axis, labelled 40, 80, 120, 160, 200) against "Al content, wt.%" (x-axis, 3 to 10). A dashed curve with filled diamonds peaks near 200 J/cm2 at about 6.5-7 wt.% Al; a solid curve with open diamonds peaks near 165 J/cm2 at similar Al content. Both curves fall steeply above 7 wt.% Al and drop to about 100 and 65 J/cm2 respectively by 10 wt.% Al. Taken together, the panels argue that solution-treated Fe-Mn-Al-C steels retain austenitic-stainless-type impact energy, that the low curves 4 and 5 correspond to aged (550 °C/16 h) material embrittled by k-carbide, and that impact toughness is maximised at intermediate Al content.

subfigures.description: Charpy impact absorbed energy (J, 0-250) versus testing temperature (°C, -200 to 100) for five numbered curves, overlaid on shaded reference bands labelled Austenite stainless steel, Dual phase steel, Ferrite steel and Martensite steel. Curves 1-3 (open symbols) show high, steeply rising energy with a transition below about -100 °C; curves 4 (filled squares) and 5 (filled triangles) stay low (< ~50 J) and approach 0 J near room temperature.

Impact toughness (J/cm2, axis labelled 40-200) versus Al content (wt.%, 3-10). Dashed curve with filled diamonds peaks near 200 J/cm2 around 6.5-7 wt.% Al; solid curve with open diamonds peaks near 165 J/cm2 at a similar Al content. Both decrease abruptly above 7 wt.% Al.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots Charpy impact absorbed energy in J (y-axis 0-250, ticks at 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250) against testing temperature in °C (x-axis -200 to 100).

Four shaded background bands in panel (a) are labelled, from top to bottom, 'Austenite stainless steel', 'Dual phase steel', 'Ferrite steel' and 'Martensite steel', providing reference toughness ranges.

In panel (a) the curves marked 1, 2 (open squares) and 3 (open diamonds) reach high absorbed energies, approaching the 200 J gridline near 0-20 °C, whereas curves 4 (filled squares) and 5 (filled triangles) remain below the 50 J gridline across the entire tested temperature range.
Curve 3 in panel (a) rises quasi-linearly from near 0 J at about -190 °C to just above the 200 J gridline at 20 °C, showing the steepest temperature dependence.
Curve 5 in panel (a) is essentially flat and close to 0 J at room temperature, the lowest impact energy of all five curves.

Panel (b) plots 'Impact toughness, J/cm2' (ticks labelled 40, 80, 120, 160, 200) against 'Al content, wt.%' from 3 to 10; two curves are shown, one dashed with filled diamonds and one solid with open diamonds.
In panel (b) the dashed (filled-diamond) curve lies above the solid (open-diamond) curve at every Al content, and both peak near 6.5-7 wt.% Al, at about the 200 and 165 J/cm2 levels respectively.

The caption states that (a) shows the relationship between Charpy impact absorbed energy and testing temperature for Fe-Mn-Al-C austenite steel [104,105] and (b) the relationship between impact toughness and Al content for Fe-Mn-Al-C steel [106].
The citing text states that aging at 550 °C for 16 h (curves 4 and 5 in Fig. 15a) greatly reduced the room-temperature impact energy, with a Fe30Mn10Al1C steel approaching 0 J.
The citing text attributes the loss of impact energy in aged Fe-Mn-Al-C steels mainly to precipitation of k-carbide.
The citing text states that when Al content is lower than 7%, k-carbide cannot precipitate but Fe3C and M7C3 may precipitate along grain boundaries during aging, reducing impact toughness.
The citing text states that at 7-10% Al the formation of Fe3C and M7C3 is inhibited but brittle k-carbide gradually precipitates along grain boundaries, also decreasing impact toughness.

The citing text states that above 10% Al, d-ferrite gradually forms and further reduces impact toughness, with microcracks generated at the austenite/ferrite phase interface due to deformation incompatibility.

The citing text states that an obvious ductile-brittle transition stage occurs in the solution-treated A-BDP steels when the testing temperature is below -100 °C, consistent with the steep drop of curves 1-3 below about -100 °C in panel (a).

panel (a): exact data-point coordinate values are not printed, only gridlines at 50 J intervals
panel (b): no numeric data labels are printed; peak positions estimated only relative to axis ticks
